Closing this — after further investigation the bug is not on the OpenCode Go side at all.

Manual `curl` requests to the OpenCode Go API with the correct model name (e.g. `minimax-m2.7`) work fine. The HTTP 401 "Model not supported" error was being caused by a bug in the Hermes Agent CLI, which was silently replacing dots with hyphens in model names before making the API request (so `minimax-m2.7` was being sent as `minimax-m2-7`).

Description
Android/Termux environments are currently treated as standard Linux in the CLI launcher, which can result in runtime failures due to incompatible binaries.
Because Termux runs in a constrained Android environment, certain assumptions made for standard Linux systems (e.g., binary compatibility, filesystem layout) do not hold.
A detection check should be added early in the launcher to identify Android/Termux environments and exit with a clear unsupported platform message.
Steps to Reproduce
Run the CLI within a Termux (Android) environment
Observe that the environment is detected as standard Linux
Attempt to execute CLI commands
Encounter runtime failures or incompatible binary execution
Expected Behavior
The CLI should detect Android/Termux environments early and exit with a clear message indicating that the platform is not yet supported.
Actual Behavior
The CLI proceeds as if running on standard Linux, which may lead to failures due to incompatible binaries.
Environment
OS: Android (Termux)
Terminal: Termux
Notes
Early environment detection would prevent unnecessary execution attempts and provide clearer feedback to users, improving overall reliability and user experience.

Same issue with BMP files. Reading a `.bmp` file sends `image/bmp` to the Anthropic API, which rejects it, and the error gets baked into the conversation history making the session unrecoverable.

The root cause is in `read.ts` — the image check is `mime.startsWith("image/")` with only SVG and fastbidsheet excluded. This lets through BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, JXL, and any other `image/*` type that providers do not support.

A minimal fix would be to allowlist the formats that providers actually accept (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`) and return an error message for unsupported formats instead of trying to encode and send them. Working on a PR for this.

This is the biggest memory hog I've seen: Opencode bootstraps a workspace when you open, hover, or expand it's parent project. Each bootstrap initializes a new MCP process based on your config for every single workspace. So if you have 5 MCPs in your config and 3 projects with 5 workspaces each, (which isn't that much), then that's 75 MCP instances running on your computer taking a significant amount of memory. A good way to test this is to add the [chome dev tools mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) and [playwright mcp](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp) to your global config and create some workspaces in the desktop app and look at your activity monitor. If you look at the codex open source code or other companies ai agent code you'd need to create some sort of MCP manager refactor to fix this. I'm not sure if this is only on the desktop app or not.
